_comment: Curated source of truth for the station/destination registry (TERC-46). The TERC report API provides names and activity; it provides NO coordinates (confirmed TERC-79 by reading the report Lambdas' own field lists) — those live here. TERC-79 reconciled three sources: TERC's own production real-time app, an older legacy station table, and OSM geocoding. Every coordinate is checked against OpenStreetMap's Lake Tahoe polygon and sits in open water; `source` records which won. `verified` still means confirmed by TERC staff for THIS project (none yet). ALL coordinates are stored at exactly 5 decimal places — see _precision.
_precision: 5 decimal places everywhere, deliberately and uniformly. At Lake Tahoe's latitude 1 degree of longitude is 86.4 km, so a coordinate rounded to 2 dp carries +/-432 m of slop and 3 of these 18 stations land on dry ground; 5 dp is +/-0.4 m. Mixed precision was the TERC-79 bug: 11 of 18 markers rendered on land. Do not 'tidy' trailing zeros away — 39.23640 must keep its zero so the column stays uniform and the class of bug cannot return.
_station_names: Names are the report API's own Station_Name values, read from GET /report/ns-stations (TERC-79). Ids 1, 3, 5 and 10 were previously placeholders ('NS Station N') — they are really Cascade, Glenbrook, Meeks and Camp Richardson. Getting id 3's name right matters: it is Glenbrook, on the EAST shore, and it had been sitting 19 km away on the south-west.

stations.name: Cascade
stations.note: ON CASCADE LAKE, not Lake Tahoe — TERC's nearshore page says the network is 10 Tahoe stations plus one on Cascade Lake. Never observed 2024-2026; absent from TERC's own production station list.

stations.name: Dollar Point
stations.source: legacy table (app value is 542 m offshore, vs 2.0 m reported depth)
stations.note: Legacy value, 83 m offshore. The production app's 39.1947,-120.089 is 542 m out, which does not square with the 2.0 m depth this station reports.

stations.name: Glenbrook
stations.note: EAST shore. Was 'NS Station 3' at 38.933,-120.025 — 19 km away on the south-west shore.

stations.name: Homewood
stations.source: legacy table (app value is 1.1 km north)
stations.note: Legacy value, 12 m offshore, matching its 2.0 m reported depth. Sits exactly on the 39.09 N midline the half-lake destinations split on — counted as north.

stations.name: Meeks
stations.note: Never observed 2024-2026; absent from TERC's own production station list. Position is Meeks Bay, 72 m offshore — best effort, needs TERC confirmation.

stations.name: Tahoe City
stations.source: derived — BOTH sources on dry land, 2.1 km apart
stations.note: BOTH sources put this on land: the app 479 m inland, the legacy table 248 m inland and 1.9 km from the village (200 m from the Cedar Point station — and that table has no Cedar Point row, so it looks like a mix-up). Derived from the OSM village centre, 73 m offshore. Needs TERC. Last seen Jan 2026.

stations.name: Camp Richardson
stations.note: Was 'NS Station 10' at 38.99,-120.105 — 880 m inland, 7 km north-west.

stations.name: Timber Cove
stations.source: derived from the Timber Cove Lodge pier — legacy inland, app 292 m out
stations.note: Legacy value is 77 m inland; the app's is 292 m offshore, far for a dock sensor. Derived from the Timber Cove Lodge pier, 72 m offshore.

stations.name: Cedar Point
stations.note: WEST shore, between Tahoe City and Homewood. The old placeholder put it at 39.225,-119.93 on the east shore, which is why it had been grouped under the Glenbrook destination.

stations.name: Homewood TC
stations.note: id-less endpoint; thermistor chain, 584 m offshore — deeper water than the dock-mounted nearshore sensors, which is expected. Last seen Apr 2026.

_destinations_comment: Station membership recomputed in TERC-79 by nearest destination, using the corrected coordinates. Two groupings had been artefacts of wrong coordinates: 'glenbrook' held station 12 (Cedar Point, actually WEST shore) instead of station 3 (Glenbrook, 0.1 km away), and 'tahoe-keys' held station 3. The half-lake destinations keep the documented rule — split at 39.09 N, the lake's E-W midline. Note Glenbrook (39.08830) falls 0.2 km SOUTH of that line, so it groups with South Lake Tahoe by the rule.
_tiebreaker: The app and the legacy table disagree by up to 2.1 km. Tiebreaker: every station that reports a depth reports 1.4-2.0 m (Depth_m4C_Avg), i.e. sensors on private docks in shallow water. So where sources conflict, take the in-water candidate CLOSEST to shore and reject any candidate on land. Result: every nearshore station now sits 12-134 m offshore. Disagreements still worth TERC's confirmation: Dollar Point (sources 1232 m apart), Homewood (1139 m), Rubicon (516 m), Timber Cove (374 m), Tahoe City (2111 m, and BOTH sources are on dry land).
